sections.html: Originating from the USA and South America, Najas guadalupensis is an exceptionally easy aquatic plant that thrives under almost any conditions. It grows quickly and propagates effortlessly, making it ideal for beginners as well as experienced aquarists.

• Common names: Guppy grass, Najas grass, Common water nymph
  • Lighting: Low to medium
  • Substrate: not needed (or any)
  • Growth form: stem
  • Growth rate: fast
  • Placement: floating
  • Size: up to 90 cm without trimming
  • Fertilizers: not needed to low
  • CO2: not needed to low
  • Propagation: by clipping the stems off
  • Colour: light green to dark green
Loài này lan rất nhanh và ở một số nơi trên thế giới đã thành cây xâm hại. Cây cắt bỏ thì đem cho, chuyển sang bể khác, hoặc vứt sao cho chim, thú không tha được nó ra ao hồ, sông suối.

Najas grass is inexpensive and readily available in local pet stores. It does not ship well because of its delicate nature and can disintegrate in transit.

Unless the plant is certainly safe (for example grown in vitro in an undamaged, unopened pot), quarantine and disinfect it with bleach or potassium permanganate. It can carry parasites, pests such as snails, or predators (dragonfly and damselfly nymphs), and may have been treated with pesticides that are extremely poisonous to fish, shrimp and other invertebrates.

Guppy grass belongs to the genus Najas, the water nymphs or naiads, a genus of about 40 aquatic plants with a cosmopolitan distribution. The genus was first described by Carl Linnaeus in 1753 and is placed in the family Hydrocharitaceae, previously Najadaceae.

Guppy grass is native to North America, where it is widespread. It is also distributed in Canada, Mexico, Central America, the Caribbean, South America and Asia.

In the wild, guppy grass is found in a wide variety of aquatic habitats, such as fast-moving to still streams, ditches, ponds, and freshwater and brackish lakes. It also grows in local waterways and canals, and is considered an invasive species in some countries.

It is an annual submerged plant with long, slender, much-branched stems that can reach a maximum height of 90 cm. The leaves are narrow, thin and flexible, up to 3 cm long and 1–2 mm wide, green, arranged oppositely in whorls and edged with tiny unicellular teeth. The plant has white roots and small inconspicuous flowers.
Muốn có một đám cây rậm phủ kín tầng dưới trong bể nhỏ hoặc vừa thì loài này làm rất dễ. Chỉ cần mua một túi nhỏ, chẳng bao lâu nó sẽ phủ kín bể.
Guppy grass can be kept even in nano tanks. However, because of how fast it grows, a minimum tank size of 40 litres is suggested.

Cách hay làm nhất với rong đuôi chồn Najas là thả nổi tự do trong bể. Muốn để nó ở hậu cảnh cũng được, vì cây tự bám xuống nền bằng những sợi rễ dài và mảnh. Nếu bể có cá bột hay tép, đám thân lá mảnh và xốp của nó là chỗ trốn tốt cho chúng.

Cây mọc thành đám xum xuê nổi trong nước, nên có lẽ không hợp với bể có dòng chảy mạnh. Thấy rậm quá thì thỉnh thoảng ngắt bớt một ít. Có cắt mạnh, bỏ đi cả mảng lớn thì cây vẫn không sao.

Cây không cần đèn đắt tiền hay lịch châm phân rắc rối. Nước bể quá mềm thì có thể châm thêm chút phân nước.
Although usually kept as a free-floating plant, it may anchor itself in the substrate with long, delicate roots.

Guppy grass can be introduced in two ways: planted in the substrate or floated in the water column. Most aquarists prefer to leave it floating. A mix of both is also possible.

To plant it, divide the stems into many pieces and root them 5 cm deep into the substrate, spacing them properly. The root system is weak and serves mainly for attachment. Guppy grass may melt if it is planted after having been floating.

To float it, divide the stems evenly and place them in the water column.

It propagates by sending off side shoots, and stems can be clipped off and either planted or left floating.

Care is simple: keep it in check so that it does not overrun the tank. A dense mass can cut off light to plants at the bottom, so trim it every few weeks, either discarding the cuttings or passing them to other hobbyists. The lower sections of the stems become unattractive as they age and should be removed periodically. Supplement the water with liquid fertiliser after water changes or when nutrients may be lacking.

Trimmings should be disposed of properly in plastic bags so they do not block local waterways and canals.
Cây hợp với pH 6–7 nhưng chịu được pH cao hơn. Nhiệt độ ở các bể cá thông thường đều ổn với nó.

Temperature: the optimal range is 20–26 °C, though the plant tolerates a wide range of temperatures.

pH: 6.0–8.0.

Hardness: it easily tolerates soft or hard water, with a tolerance range of 2–20 GH.

Water flow: the plant flourishes in lower flow. It grows better, and does not clog the filter and make a mess of the tank as it does in fast-flowing water.

Substrate: guppy grass is mainly a floating plant, but it can be rooted in a variety of substrates. It does not require a nutrient-rich substrate. Whichever way it is planted, make sure there are sufficient nutrients in the tank water.

Lighting: it does well in low to medium light, ideally on for at least 8 and at most 12 hours daily. The more light (closer to medium) it has, the greener it will be. Under high light it gets a reddish tint, and high light might also burn it.

Fertilisation and CO2: it can thrive without CO2 injection, but liquid carbon can be dosed if the plants are struggling. Fertiliser is essential to replenish lost nutrients, and liquid fertilisers from time to time are recommended. Even if planted, root tabs are not needed, as the plant takes nutrients mainly from the water column.

If you keep shrimp with guppy grass, note that a high level of CO2 and copper (most fertilisers contain copper) is extremely dangerous to shrimp.

Cá con của cá đẻ con trốn trong đám cây còn kiếm được vi sinh vật và trùng cỏ để ăn. Cá nhỏ và tép thích loài cây này vì có chỗ ẩn, có mồi để rỉa và có bóng râm che bớt ánh đèn mạnh từ trên chiếu xuống. Một người nuôi thấy đám cây lên nhanh làm cảnh trong bể luôn thay đổi, cá tò mò hơn và có chỗ nghỉ thoải mái.

Guppy grass is best suited to guppies, but is also a great choice for community tanks with small freshwater fish such as Otocinclus catfish, pygmy corydoras, ember tetra, neon tetras, green fire tetra, cardinal fish, celestial pearl danios, zebra danios and platies; dwarf shrimp of virtually any species, which graze on it and hide in it; and snails such as ramshorn, nerite, Malaysian trumpet, Japanese trapdoor and mystery snails.

It is compatible with most plants and animals that prefer low light. However, some snails and herbivorous fish such as plecos, goldfish, cichlids, rosy barbs, silver dollars and tilapia are likely to feed on it. It is also a good choice for freshwater crab and crayfish tanks.
Nhân giống chỉ cần ngắt một phần đám cây đem sang bể khác. Cây mọc nhanh nên lúc nào cũng có phần dư để chia cho bạn bè.

The fine, porous structure provides excellent shelter for fish fry and shrimp, while also helping to absorb excess nutrients and produce oxygen. Perfect for both aquariums and ponds, Najas guadalupensis supports a healthy, balanced environment and offers a natural hiding place for aquatic life.

Ngoài phần dinh dưỡng dư, cây còn hút nitrat, amoni và cả kim loại nặng trong nước. Nó giành dinh dưỡng với rêu hại, nên rêu khó bùng lên hơn. Một người nuôi thấy đây là loại cây hợp nhất cho bể nhỏ, vì cây lên nhanh và lọc bớt chất dư trong nước, lỡ bể có trục trặc thì cũng yên tâm hơn.

Benefits: it provides hiding places and shelter for fry; removes ammonia, nitrate, nitrite and heavy metals; offers breeding ground for shrimp, livebearers and egg scatterers; serves as food for herbivores such as silver dollars, herbivorous cichlids and goldfish; competes with algae for nutrients and so reduces algae; promotes oxygenation; adds dense green foliage; and hosts biofilm, an ideal first food for newly hatched fry and shrimplets.

Problems: rapid growth can overrun the tank and block light from plants at the bottom (although this can help if you keep low-light plants). The stems are fragile and break easily, but broken parts develop new side shoots. It may melt after being introduced to the tank because of changed growing conditions, and needs time to adapt.
